name: Encrypted dedication, Richard Powers, The Gold Bug Variations (1991)
ciphertext: RLS CMW DJP RFP J?O CEP JJN PRG ZTS MCJ
JEH BLM CRR PLC JCM MEP JNH JDM RBS J?H
BJP PJP SCB TLC KES REP RCP DTH I?H CRB
ciphertext_source: Cipherbrain post 22 (Schmeh 2017, sources/schmeh/posts/22-powers.txt), from the printed dedication page; 32 triplets, three with a '?' as middle letter.
alphabet: capital letters in 32 triplets (96 positions, 3 unknown)

constraints.structure_hint: the Goldberg Variations are aria + 30 variations + aria da capo = 32 movements; the novel is built on them and on the 64 DNA codons; J appears 19 times, mostly first or middle
constraints.not_amino_acids: J, O and B occur, which are not amino-acid one-letter codes
constraints.hypothesis_on_record: Stefan Wagner (Cipherbrain 2015): initials of 32 people; JSB = Johann Sebastian Bach

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Print check first (rule 1): J. T. Thomas, 'Deciphering the code in Richard Powers's The Gold Bug Variations' (thefreelibrary id a0159331538; the article's own title claims a decipherment; the cloud gets 403, so an owner-machine row) and Powers scholarship in the open indexes. Cost $1.

2. Structural test: align the 32 triplets with the 32 movements and with the novel's chapter list (30 chapters plus frame); test whether each triplet is the initials of a chapter title, a Goldberg canon interval, or a dedicatee named in the acknowledgements. Cost $2, Sonnet, needs the chapter list (Wikipedia/Google Books preview).
3. Initials test: the 32 triplets against the people in Powers's acknowledgements and biography; 'J?O', 'J?H' suggest middle names unknown to the dedicator. Cost $1.
matched_control: 32 random triplets from the initial-letter distribution of English names, same alignment tests
value: moderate; the author is alive and the answer is presumably known to him; a print check may close it at N0/N1
status_24_Sept_2026: open per Schmeh 2017; Bourdeau: 'not settleable by cryptanalysis'; print check pending
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run is under cheap_test_done with its control
